Formulation:
A 26-year-old female teacher experiencing increased stress related to work pressures and long hours, contributing to fatigue. Concurrent acute onset of dry, itchy, red rash localized mainly to hands and arms started a few days after swimming, consistent with irritant or allergic contact dermatitis triggered by pool chemicals; family history of atopy may predispose to atopic dermatitis. Stress may exacerbate skin symptoms or precipitate eczema. No prior history of skin disease; no systemic symptoms reported. Protective factors include stable general health and no substance use. Presentation involves interaction of environmental triggers, occupational stressors, and possible atopic predisposition.

Mental Health Care Plan Details

Principal Problem: Work-related stress and fatigue
- Patient Goal(s): To reduce work-related stress and improve energy levels
- Clinical Goal(s): Identify stress management strategies; monitor fatigue; support coping mechanisms to prevent worsening mental health
- Actions (Patient): Implement stress reduction techniques (e.g., time management, breaks); consider discussing workload with employer
- Actions (Clinician/GP): Provide psychological support or refer to counseling if stress persists; monitor mental status and fatigue

Secondary Problem: Irritant or allergic contact dermatitis
- Patient Goal(s): Resolution of rash and relief of itchiness
- Clinical Goal(s): Alleviate skin inflammation and discomfort; prevent worsening or complications
- Actions (Patient): Apply prescribed emollients and steroid creams as directed; consider over-the-counter antihistamines for itch relief; avoid known irritants (e.g., pool chemicals)
- Actions (Clinician/GP): Prescribe topical corticosteroids and emollients; provide patient information leaflet on dermatitis; advise on use of antihistamines; schedule follow-up if no improvement in one week

Patient Education, Emergency Care & Relapse Prevention:
- Education Given: Yes. Topics Covered: Nature of dermatitis, treatment options (topical steroids, emollients, antihistamines), role of environmental triggers, impact of stress on skin
- Early Warning Signs of Relapse/Worsening: Increasing redness, spread of rash, cracked skin, development of systemic symptoms such as fever
- Coping Strategies: Emollient use, stress management, avoiding irritants, early re-presentation if symptoms persist or worsen

- Copy of Mental Health Care Plan Given to Patient: Not recorded
- Other Mental Health Professionals Involved in Patient Care: None recorded

- Review Date: Recommend follow-up in 1 week for skin and stress reassessment

Summary of Differential Diagnoses (from DDx)
- Irritant or allergic contact dermatitis — High likelihood; supported by acute onset post-swimming, localized rash, absence of systemic symptoms
- Atopic dermatitis (new onset) — Medium likelihood; family history of atopy and stress as contributory factors
- Xerosis (dry skin) due to environmental causes — Medium likelihood; patient suspects weather may play a role; less likely given acute onset and redness indicating inflammation
